title: "Fragment serializing algorithm" outputs node itself instead of its contents for elements in non-HTML documents
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The "fragment serializing algorithm" behavior is differerent for HTML and non-HTML elements.

The [`innerHTML`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#dom-element-innerhtml) property getter expects this algorithm to return *contents* of the passed element:
> [Element](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element)'s innerHTML getter steps are to return the result of running [fragment serializing algorithm steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dynamic-markup-insertion.html#fragment-serializing-algorithm-steps) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and true.

Then, the non-HTML branch of *fragment serializing algorithm* "calls" *XML serialization*:

> 1. Let context document be node's [node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document).
> 2. If context document is an [HTML document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document), return the result of [HTML fragment serialization algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#html-fragment-serialisation-algorithm) with node, false, and « ».
> 3. **Return the [XML serialization](https://w3c.github.io/DOM-Parsing/#dfn-xml-serialization) of node given require well-formed.**

Then, XML serialization (almost) directly "calls" [XML serializing an Element node](https://w3c.github.io/DOM-Parsing/#dfn-xml-serializing-an-element-node), which can be seen to generate serialization of the node itself instead of its contents.

Example testcase:
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<script>
    const svgstr = `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">PASS</svg>`;
    const svg = new DOMParser().parseFromString(svgstr, "image/svg+xml").documentElement;
    console.log(svg.innerHTML);
</script>
```
On mainstream engines (Blink, Gecko), this prints `PASS`. If implemented as written in the spec, this would cause`svg.innerHTML` to actually return "outer HTML" for it (`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">PASS</svg>`).
